row.evidence: Common Room's pricing table checks "SAML/SCIM Security" on Essential, Advanced and Enterprise, and its SCIM guide says "You can provision user accounts in the Common Room application through SCIM."
row.notes: No free plan; the cheapest plan, Essential, is $2,500/mo billed annually with 5 seats, so per-seat fields stay null (flat pricing). SAML/SCIM Security is checked on all three plans. The SCIM and SAML docs still say 'Team and Enterprise plans' (older plan names), see conflicts. SCIM is documented only as an Okta OIN app (create, update, deactivate, Group Push to roles); the security page says SCIM also works with Azure AD but no Entra guide or generic base URL is published. Deactivation turns the user into a Contact. The public API covers Contacts, not teammates. Audit events stream to S3 on Enterprise.

plans.name: Essential
plans.notes: SAML/SCIM Security and SSO (GSuite, GitHub) rows carry a checkmark icon in all three plan columns of the comparison table.

auth.token_source: Settings > API Tokens > Add another account > create a new token (Admin profile required)
auth.notes: The token is an ordinary Common Room API token pasted into Okta's API Token field; the auth scheme and expiry are not documented.

operations.notes: Docs list Creating Users, Updating User Attributes, Deactivating Users, permission assignment and role management via SCIM Groups (Okta Group Push). PUT vs PATCH not stated.

deprovision.data_retained: The user is converted to a Contact in the room (record kept).

custom.how: Okta app custom attribute 'Common Room Role' (Admin, Editor or Viewer permission) set on assignment

attributes.notes: Only the email username, the Common Room Role custom attribute and group displayName are named; no full attribute list is published.

roles.how: Permission level (Admin/Editor/Viewer) via the Common Room Role attribute; in-app roles via SCIM Groups whose displayName matches an existing Common Room role

limitations.text: Changing a user's email creates a new Common Room account instead of updating the existing one.
Group Push does not create roles; a role with the same name must already exist in Common Room.
Roles assigned manually in the UI are not tracked or reconciled by SCIM groups.
Only an Okta setup guide is published; the security page says SCIM works via multiple IdPs including Azure AD, but no Entra guide or base URL is documented.

scim.notes: SCIM is set up through Okta's OIN app; no generic SCIM base URL is published. Common Room does not write attributes back to Okta.

audit_log_api.notes: Security audit events (sign-in, role assigned/revoked, seat added/removed, API token created/revoked) are streamed in OCSF format to a customer S3 bucket on Enterprise; this is a push export, not a query API.

limitations.text: Teammates are invited and assigned permissions in Settings > Team Access in the UI.

user_api.notes: The Common Room API manages Contacts, activities, organizations, segments and tags (GET /contacts, POST /contacts/bulk and similar) plus GET /me for the token's user. No endpoint for workspace users (teammates), permissions or roles was found in the v2 reference, so no user-management API is recorded.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate and Group Push as supported (checkmark classes in the page markup).

entra.notes: Common Room's security page names Azure AD for SAML and SCIM, but no Entra gallery tutorial was found (learn.microsoft.com common-room tutorial URLs 404).

fallbacks.notes: SAML SSO is configured by sending the IdP metadata URL to Common Room support. Docs also offer Google Workspace and GitHub sign-in. JIT and CSV import of teammates not documented.

conflicts.text: The SCIM and SAML docs say SCIM and SAML are included on 'Team and Enterprise plans', older plan names; the current pricing page has Essential, Advanced and Enterprise and checks SAML/SCIM Security on all three.

open_questions: SCIM base URL, auth scheme and token expiry are not documented (setup is through Okta's OIN app).
No Entra, Google, OneLogin or JumpCloud SCIM guide found, although the security page names Azure AD.
Docs do not say whether deactivation frees the seat or ends active sessions, or whether delete is supported.
Whether any plan name 'Team' still exists (docs) versus Essential/Advanced/Enterprise (pricing).
